# 51.05 - Carry a blank line from the manifest into the generated file

## Objective

Let an author group entries without inventing a nesting level, by making a blank
line between two entries of `scripts` or `files` a group boundary that reaches
the generated `meta.xml` at the same place.

## Why this is worth its cost

The authored `meta.xml` this milestone is built from has three section comments
over seven visual blocks. The blocks carry the meaning — libraries together,
the utility pair together, the service pair together — and the comments are
coarser than they are. Any field-based grouping would either force a comment on
every block or add a level of nesting to the manifest to hold a group that has
no other property. A blank line is what the author already types, and it already
means exactly this.

The cost is real and is stated so nobody meets it by surprise: this is the one
construct in the manifest with no value of its own, and it makes whitespace
load-bearing in two lists. Every consumer must agree about it — the parser, the
evaluator, the emitter and the formatter.

## Scope

- **In:** Blank runs between entries of `scripts` and `files`, their survival
  through evaluation, their emission, and the formatter's obligation.
- **Out:** Blank lines anywhere else in the manifest, which stay meaningless, and
  authored comment text, which is not carried.

## The rule

- One or more blank lines between two entries is one boundary. Two blank lines
  are not two boundaries; the generated file gets one blank line.
- A blank line before the first entry or after the last is not a boundary and is
  dropped.
- A comment line between entries is not a boundary and is not carried.
- A boundary is a property of the *gap*, so it survives an entry being edited and
  disappears with the entry only if the gap closes.

## Steps

- [ ] Record, for each entry of an ordered list, whether a blank run precedes it.
      The parser already carries positions; the gap is derivable from the line of
      the previous entry's last token and the line of this entry's first token,
      so no new syntax node is needed.
- [ ] Carry the flag through evaluation into the entry value, and through
      discovery and assembly to the manifest script and file entries.
- [ ] Emit one blank line before the first element produced by an entry that
      opens a boundary, and never before the first element of a section.
- [ ] Make the formatter preserve blank runs between entries of these two lists,
      collapse a run of two or more to one, and never introduce one. Add the rule
      to `.luam.formatter`'s documented behaviour, not to its options: a manifest
      whose layout depends on a formatter setting is a manifest that formats
      differently on two machines.
- [ ] Add `format --check` coverage so a manifest that round-trips through the
      formatter produces a byte-identical `meta.xml`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A blank line between two `scripts` entries produces a blank line between
      their elements, at the same place.
- [ ] Two blank lines produce one.
- [ ] A blank line before the first entry or after the last produces nothing.
- [ ] A comment between two entries produces neither a blank line nor a comment.
- [ ] Deleting a blank line merges the blocks and changes nothing else.
- [ ] `luam format` on any fixture manifest leaves its generated `meta.xml`
      byte-identical, verified as a test rather than by inspection.
- [ ] The `heaven-roleplay` fixture's blank lines land exactly where the authored
      file has them.
